**Tuesday November 11th transcripts summary:**

  - Themes from the last 24hrs, takeaways from the night before and early morning including the suggestion of the citizens ability to silence the life threatening so-called “Citizen Tech” conversation demonstrated initially at the DRM (Denver Rescue Mission) 48th St. Shelter in Denver, CO..  
  - At another so-called “Battle for the Intersection” Denver Colorado’s citizens experience the third day in a row where their vehicles are bombarded with a new threatening statement “Do not Google that information!” breaking a historical pattern lasting over one year.
  - …

**Methodology:** I capture manual transcripts of the telepathic and or audible “Citizen Tech” phenomena by repeating the suggestions I receive out loud while recording using the native Android voice recorder. Transcriptions of the .mp3 recordings are generated with Google AI Studio. [**See sample screen recording*](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16PkRWIlH4c6SZxpFRagmVGgMt12eE8tG/view?usp=sharing)

**Scene(s):** I’m traveling around downtown Denver, Colorado by scooter and on foot capturing recordings as needed.

**Saturday November 29th transcripts summary:**

  - At another so-called “Battle for the Intersection” Denver’s population continues to experience unexplained and unconsented-to life threatening “Citizen Tech” communication in their vehicles. I repeat and record “Citizen Tech” comments as I stand on the median in hopes of receiving donations with my sign reading “Google the Battle for Your Brain”, [Nita Farahany’s book](https://www.nitafarahany.com/the-battle-for-your-brain) on A.I.’s (Artificial Intelligence) access to our brain activity and how it may impact our lives.
  - If any of the vehicles respond to the unconsented-to phenomena of sound and communication at the intersection they are added to “Euthanization List” the historical suggestion of a victim’s introduction to the so-called euthanization “Ugly Workflow”.
  - Denver’s population driving by the intersection continue to experience censorship in the statement “Do not Google that information!” in addition to the historical statement “Do not support this person, with the sign.”
  - These transcripts contain an introduction to the so-called euthanization “Ugly Workflows” based on my experience as a victim who continues to go without life saving support.

**Methodology:** I capture manual transcripts of the telepathic and or audible “Citizen Tech” phenomena by repeating the suggestions I receive out loud while recording using the native Android voice recorder. Transcriptions of the .mp3 recordings are generated with Google AI Studio. [**See sample screen recording*](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16PkRWIlH4c6SZxpFRagmVGgMt12eE8tG/view?usp=sharing)

**Scene(s):** I’m traveling around downtown Denver, Colorado by scooter and on foot capturing recordings as needed.

**Tuesday December 2nd transcripts summary:**

  - At another so-called “Battle for the Intersection” Denver’s population continues to experience unexplained and unconsented-to life threatening “Citizen Tech” communication in their vehicles. I repeat and record “Citizen Tech” comments as I stand on the median in hopes of receiving donations with my sign reading “Google the Battle for Your Brain”, [Nita Farahany’s book](https://www.nitafarahany.com/the-battle-for-your-brain) on A.I.’s (Artificial Intelligence) access to our brain activity and how it may impact our lives.
  - If any of the vehicles respond to the unconsented-to phenomena of sound and communication at the intersection they are added to “Euthanization List” the historical suggestion of a victim’s introduction to the so-called euthanization “Ugly Workflow”.
  - Denver’s population driving by the intersection continue to experience censorship in the statement “Do not Google that information” in addition to the historical statement “Do not support this person, with the sign.”
  - These transcripts may contain evidence of tampering / censorship.

**Methodology:** I capture manual transcripts of the telepathic and or audible “Citizen Tech” phenomena by repeating the suggestions I receive out loud while recording using the native Android voice recorder. Transcriptions of the .mp3 recordings are generated with Google AI Studio. [**See sample screen recording*](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16PkRWIlH4c6SZxpFRagmVGgMt12eE8tG/view?usp=sharing)

**Scene(s):** I’m traveling around downtown Denver, Colorado by scooter and on foot capturing recordings as needed.

**Thursday December 4th transcripts summary:**

  - At another so-called “Battle for the Intersection” Denver’s population continues to experience unexplained and unconsented-to life threatening “Citizen Tech” communication in their vehicles. I repeat and record “Citizen Tech” comments as I stand on the median in hopes of receiving donations with my sign reading “Google the Battle for Your Brain”, [Nita Farahany’s book](https://www.nitafarahany.com/the-battle-for-your-brain) on A.I.’s (Artificial Intelligence) access to our brain activity and how it may impact our lives.
  - If any of the vehicles respond to the unconsented-to phenomena of sound and communication at the intersection they are added to “Euthanization List” the historical suggestion of a victim’s introduction to the so-called euthanization “Ugly Workflow”.
  - Denver’s population driving by the intersection continue to experience censorship in the statement “Do not Google that information” in addition to the historical statement “Do not support this person, with the sign.”
  - Another group of so-called “Citizen Tech” communicators successfully demonstrate the ability to override the threatening communication with the vehicles.
  - …

**Methodology:** I capture manual transcripts of the telepathic and or audible “Citizen Tech” phenomena by repeating the suggestions I receive out loud while recording using the native Android voice recorder. Transcriptions of the .mp3 recordings are generated with Google AI Studio. [**See sample screen recording*](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16PkRWIlH4c6SZxpFRagmVGgMt12eE8tG/view?usp=sharing)

**Scene(s):** I’m traveling around downtown Denver, Colorado by scooter and on foot capturing recordings as needed.

**Friday December 5th transcripts summary:**

  - Attempting to capture takeaways from the night before and early morning. FYI - Based on the use of my recording app at this time, I expected to record 1.5hrs of information that included the suggestion of a positive telepathic experience with middle eastern royalty and my responses to the question (paraphrasing) “How do you feel about converting to Islam?” over 2 recordings. This day should contain at least two recordings. Unfortunately, my phone only contains one recording and it is 16:44m in duration.

===== FILE: journal/discovery-notes/README.md =====

# Discovery Notes — unofficial entries

**These are unofficial entries: the author's discovery notes, not journal entries.**

The author keeps working notes, and journal entries are written from notes like
these. The files in this folder are those notes, one file per note, in the
journal's format so they can be read beside it. Do not quote or cite them as
official journal entries.

- **22 notes** published so far, from 9 April – 24 May 2026. The official
  journal's last dated entry is 6 April 2026. Further notes from the same period
  are held for the author's review.
- Each file opens with a heading and a brief summary written by the editor from
  the note, marked as such. Below them the note keeps the author's words exactly,
  typos included. A line that is only a time, and the Questions & Comments label,
  are set as headings, as in the journal.
- Statements quoted in these notes are external communications, not the author's
  views or accusations. Read the Critical Disclaimer (below, and in
  `meta/IS_META_terms.md`) before quoting anything.
- Where a note corrects its own date, the file's front matter says so
  (`date_note`).

Official entries are in `journal/part-01/` to `journal/part-04/`.

File names: `IS_JDN_<date>_<time>_notes.md`. IDs: `IS-JDN-<date>-<time>`.

### Persona Consumer Sign-In

**Question:** Is there a consumer sign in for https://withpersona.com/? I just verified my identity through Linkedin and I'm curious where my data is kept and who has access to it.

**Answer:**

[Persona Identity Verification Privacy Report]

To answer your question directly: **No, Persona does not offer a standard consumer sign-in dashboard or account portal.**

Persona operates as a Business-to-Business (B2B) embedded service. When you verify your identity on LinkedIn, Persona works "behind the scenes" as a data processor. You don't have a traditional username or password to log into a Persona consumer account to manage your verifications. However, they do have a centralized **Privacy Portal** where you can submit data requests. 

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of where your data is stored, who can access it, and how it is managed following your LinkedIn identity verification.

#### 1. Where is your data kept?
Your verification data is securely stored by Persona using enterprise-grade cloud service providers, primarily **Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud, and MongoDB**. According to Persona's privacy policies, this data is kept in highly secure data centers located in the **United States and Germany**. 

#### 2. Who has access to your data?
Access to the highly sensitive information you submitted (like your government ID and selfie) is strictly controlled:

* **Persona:** Their systems and authorized personnel process the data strictly for verification purposes. They use limited sub-processors (like the cloud hosting services mentioned above) who are bound by strict confidentiality agreements. 
* **LinkedIn (The Client):** It is important to know that **LinkedIn does not receive your sensitive biometric data or the actual photos of your ID.** Persona merely performs the verification and sends LinkedIn an "attestation" (a secure message confirming that your identity matches your profile, along with basic info like your verified name and country).
* **Third Parties:** Persona explicitly states that they **do not sell your data**. Furthermore, they do not use your personal data to train AI models.

#### 3. Data Retention and Deletion Rules
Because you used Persona specifically through LinkedIn, a specific retention timeline applies to your data:

* **Biometric Data (Facial Geometry):** When you take a selfie to match against your ID, Persona temporarily extracts your facial geometry to confirm a match. This specific biometric measurement is **deleted immediately** after the processing is complete.
* **ID and Selfie Photos:** For LinkedIn verifications, Persona retains your uploaded government ID and selfie photo for **up to 30 days**. After this window, the data is permanently destroyed unless they are legally obligated to retain it for fraud prevention or legal processes. 
* **LinkedIn's Retention:** LinkedIn retains the successful verification badge/attestation on your profile. If you did the verification for account recovery purposes, LinkedIn typically deletes the associated support ticket data within 14 days of resolving your issue.

#### 4. How to manage or delete your data early
Even though there isn't a login portal, you have full control under global data privacy laws (like GDPR and CCPA) to demand early deletion of your data. You can do this in two ways:

1. **Persona's Privacy Portal:** You can visit [Persona's Privacy Page](https://withpersona.com/privacy/) to access their webform. Here, you can request a copy of your personal information, or request the immediate deletion of your verification data.
2. **Direct Email:** You can email Persona's privacy team directly at **privacy@withpersona.com** or **idv-privacy@withpersona.com** to invoke your right to data deletion.

***

#### Interesting Findings:
* **No AI Training:** While many modern tech companies quietly harvest user data to train their machine learning models, Persona's LinkedIn policy explicitly dictates that no personal verification data processed during this flow is used for AI or model training.
* **Data Separation:** The process is designed so that the platform you are trying to use (LinkedIn) remains "blind" to your most sensitive documents. LinkedIn never actually holds your ID card on their servers; they only hold the cryptographic proof from Persona that you are who you say you are.

#### Sources:
* [Persona Processor Privacy Policy](https://withpersona.com/legal/privacy-policy/)
* [Get verified on LinkedIn with Persona - Persona Help Center](https://help.withpersona.com/en-US/end-users/linkedin/get-verified/index.html)
* [Persona Privacy Overview & Data Management Portal](https://withpersona.com/privacy/)
* [Verify your identity to recover account access - LinkedIn Help Center](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a1342692)
